messages:
raja: quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we aggressively minimize the public API key surface for new internal services. TL;DR: prefer short-lived service tokens + mTLS for long-lived connections, keep API keys only for external customer SDKs. thoughts?

emily: +1 on minimizing. can you call out migration path for existing long-lived keys? we still have a few internal jobs using them.

raja: yes — migration plan idea: 1) introduce ephemeral token minting endpoint 2) add a compatibility proxy that accepts old API keys and exchanges for ephemeral tokens (audit only) 3) rotate keys and deprecate proxy after 90 days.

chun: question: how do we handle RBAC during the exchange? we need to preserve the original key's intent/scopes.

raja: plan is to keep scope claims on the minted token. proxy will validate original key and emit same scopes in the minted claim, plus an "orig_key_id" audit claim. no scope widening allowed.

olga: MFA angle: for some sensitive operations (key creation, granting "admin" scopes) we should require an approval step or at least an owner confirmation. do we want a hard MFA requirement or an opt-in flag per-project?

emily: prefer opt-in per-project initially. forced MFA for org-admin roles. requires console + API support.

chun: perf note: the proxy exchange path will add latency. can we avoid a hop for most internal services? maybe mint tokens in CI/deploy step and store in vault with short TTL so services read directly.

raja: exactly — for internal infra -> do direct mint during deploy and store in Vault (TTL 1h). proxy mainly for human/backwards compatibility flows.

olga: security question: how do we audit usage post-exchange? need linkage from ephemeral token back to original API key and user. the "orig_key_id" claim helps but ensure logs index it.

raja: will add structured logging: token_mint: {orig_key_id, minted_token_id, requester, reason}. auth-bot will emit an event when exchange occurs.

auth-bot: [automated] token-exchange event recorded: orig_key_id=key_7f3a, minted_token_id=tok_a12b, requester=emily, policy=read-only

emily: couple implementation details — 1) the compatibility proxy should enforce rate limits and CSRF protections 2) rotate the proxy certs regularly

chun: also recommend we add a "no-export" claim flag so some tokens cannot be exchanged (for high-value keys we might ban migration).

raja: good idea. add "migratable": true/false to key metadata. default true for low-risk, false for org-admin keys.

olga: rollout plan suggestion: create an alpha with one team, add eval metrics (latency, token churn, audit completeness), and a canary deprecation window for old keys.

raja: agreed. i'll draft a short RFC with API examples and a migration checklist. posting sample exchange API here: 

```
POST /internal/v1/token/exchange
Headers: Authorization: ApiKey key_XXXX
Body: {"ttl_seconds":3600, "reason":"migrate-job-xyz"}
Response: {"token":"ey...","expires_at":"2026-10-01T12:34:56Z","claims":{"scopes":["read:models"], "orig_key_id":"key_XXXX"}}
```

emily: nit: please include a link to the console page for manual exchanges and a flag to force "require_approver=true" for some projects.

raja: will do. i'll also add a checklist for deleting old keys and alerting owners. thanks all — i'll ping once RFC is up for review. :thumbsup:

auth-bot: [automated] raja uploaded draft RFC: /rfc/minimize-api-surface-4921234567 (permissions: eng-security read)

olga: leaving notes for the RFC: 1) make escalation path explicit 2) telemetry fields we need 3) a backwards compatibility kill-switch

chun: thanks — will test the token minting lib in my staging cluster next week and share perf numbers.

emily: great. can we also add a short FAQ for customers explaining why we removed some API key options? customer comms team will need that.

raja: yep — I'll include a customer FAQ and internal runbook. end thread.
